answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an adversary who spins up 244 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 235 times the capital for one share. The canyon report shows the merge explicitly at each yarrow. The fee repeats 6 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
